what_i_did: Hero only (no turnaround). views/hero.png is the MJ hero keyed by hue (make_views.py): the orange pot kept, the cream backdrop and the browner cast shadow dropped, the loop of the handle left open.

hero_check.py renders from +X (yaw 90 deg off the front, so the -Y spout points left as in the hero) and 10 deg up, with the harness lens and distance. A yaw/elevation grid on the round-1 model preferred 85 deg / 0 to 5 deg by a hair (0.863 vs 0.854), but the hero plainly shows the open top and the underside ellipse of the foot, so I kept 90/10 by eye and held it fixed.

One 16-segment lathe: a two-step foot ring (r 0.073 then 0.063 m), a near-spherical belly (r 0.114 m, centre 0.128 m, 4 % squashed), almost no neck, a thick rolled lip (r 0.079 m) around an open top, an inside wall and a shallow floor. Vertices carry a 1 mm seeded wobble and everything is flat-shaded, which gives the hero's soft hand-made faceting without a texture.

An 8-sided tube swept along a Catmull-Rom centreline measured off the hero: it leaves the lower front of the belly 0.08 m up with a 0.04 m radius, rises steeply, then flattens to the tip at 0.24 m, tapering to 0.011 m, with a small flared rose and a recessed mouth.
A 0.0125 m round tube (8 sides) from inside the front of the rim, up and over the back to 0.35 m, and down into the back of the belly at 0.13 m.
The pot is stretched 1.08 in plan (xy_scale), keeping the height: the hero's pot reads wider than tall, and this was the single biggest IoU gain.

1,142 triangles (budget 2k), 3 meshes (pot_body, spout, handle), one material Clay_Glaze (role clay), flat base colour, no textures, no animation. 0.36 m tall to the handle top, 0.47 m long spout tip to handle back, origin at the centre of the base on the ground, spout to -Y.
good: Hero silhouette IoU 0.886 from the hero's direction: belly, foot ring, rolled lip, the long rising spout and the high loop handle all line up.
Reads at tile size as a round orange watering pot: the spout and the big loop are the two silhouette features and both are thick enough to survive.
off: The hero's spout leaves the belly as a broad flattened fillet; mine is a round tube that thickens into the belly, so the joint is a little narrower at the bottom.
The hero's handle is a perfectly smooth tube; at 16 steps mine shows its segments at the top of the arch.
The hero's glaze has specular highlights and painterly mottling; mine is one flat colour with geometric faceting only.
The spout rises at about 40 to 45 deg near the body and about 25 deg near the tip in the hero, so I followed the hero rather than a straight 30 deg.
The hero camera was set by eye and only checked against a calibration grid on the round-1 model, so the hero number is a guide.

rounds.change: First build from pixel measurements: 20-segment lathe, bezier spout, handle loop. Camera fixed at 90/10.
Spout and handle centrelines re-measured off the hero, 16 segments: everything above the foot came out too high relative to the width.
Plan stretched 1.08 (xy_scale), handle loop 10 % taller and leaned 2 cm forward, spout centreline 12 mm lower (from a small parameter sweep).
Foot ring 6 % narrower, darker glaze sampled from the shaded belly, steadier handle tube.
Triangles 1,382 -> 1,142: fewer belly rings, a 5-point lip, 16 handle and 9 spout steps.
Final 768 px / 48 sample render and score; to_game.py watering-pot.

moving_parts: None: a static garden prop, exported with export_animations=False.
creative_additions: A recessed mouth in the spout rose and a shallow floor inside the open top, so the top reads as open from the tile's high camera.
